unsettled: English Schedule-I readable only to entry 60. WebFetch's text of the consolidated PDFs stops inside entry 38 (Pakistan Code, 'Updated till 04.08.2023') and inside entry 60 (SJA, 'Updated till 05.08.2023'). Rows after entry 60 were read only in the Pakistan Code Urdu text, which prints the substance names in Latin script but no serial numbers and no date. So MDA (tenamfetamine), PCP, psilocybin and the THC rows have no entry number, and any footnotes in that part of the 2023 consolidations were not seen. A browser read of pages 46-50 of the Pakistan Code PDF would settle this.

Delta-9-THC (dronabinol), kept draft: in the Urdu text, the chemical name the UN schedules give for dronabinol is printed beside SECOBARBITAL, with no Latin-script name. The separate row 'tetrahydrocannabinol, the following isomers and their stereochemical variants' lists six other isomers. The English row's name and number were not reached.

Lorazepam: entry 44 is printed 'LOPRAZEPAM' (sic) in both the SJA and the Urdu texts, between LOPRAZOLAM (43) and LORMETAZEPAM (45). The Urdu text gives it lorazepam's chemical name; the SJA text repeats lormetazepam's. Recorded as lorazepam; editor to confirm.

Synthetic and semi-synthetic opioids: fentanyl and its analogues, methadone, oxycodone, hydrocodone, codeine, tramadol and tapentadol are not named in the Act's definitions or in Schedule-I (buprenorphine is entry 7). s. 2(q)(ii) lets the Federal Government declare 'any other narcotic substance' a manufactured drug by Gazette notification; none was found. The Gazette search system (drs.molaw.gov.pk) and ANF's library (which holds a file 'S.R.O. 597(I)/97' under ACTS) refuse robots, and the 'CNS Rules 2001' named on the Ministry of Narcotics Control's Publications page could not be located as a file. These rows stay draft; the editor should obtain those notifications and Rules before publishing them as 'not controlled'.

Schedule-II (precursors, Divisions I and II = Tables I and II of the 1988 Convention) exists only in the 2022 Gazette, whose OCR is too garbled for a full list. The legible entries are precursor chemicals; none of the 77 items.
Schedule notes not read: SJA prints 'MIDAZOLAM**' and the Urdu text 'MIDAZOLAM***'; the notes these markers point to, and any closing clause (for example on salts), were not reached.

Unnumbered rows (no serial number in any copy read; recorded as 'unnumbered row printed after entry N'): DET, DMA and DMHP (after 12); DMT and DOET (after 13); MDMA, mescaline, 4-methylaminorex, MMDA, N-ethyl MDA, N-hydroxy MDA, parahexyl, PMA and psilocine (after 41); levomethamphetamine (after 46). Butobarbital (after 11) is in the Pakistan Code English and Urdu texts but not in SJA's.
